utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Could you call the case, please, Madam Registrar. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. This is the case number, IT-99-36-T, the Prosecutor versus Radoslav Brdjanin and Momir Talic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Mr. Brdjanin, good morning to you. Can you hear me in a language that you can understand.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED BRDJANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, Your Honour. I can hear you and I understand you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I thank you. General Talic, can you hear me in a language that you can understand?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED TALIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, Your Honour, I can hear you in a language that I understand.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Appearances for the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Joanna Korner, assisted by Susan Grogan case manager. Good morning, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I thank you. And good morning to you. Appearances for Mr. Brdjanin.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. I'm John Ackerman with Tania Radosavljevic and Marela Jevtovic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Good morning to you. Appearances for General Talic.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU-IVANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Natasha Fauveau-Ivanovic assisted by Fabien Masson. I represent General Talic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. Any preliminaries.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Your Honour, only this, I had a look yesterday at the motion by Mr. Ackerman asking for a certification on the Rule 70 matter. Your Honour, effectively I think the Prosecution take a neutral view. We think the judgement is correct, and we don't resile from it. But if Your Honours feel that Mr. Ackerman's application that this is a matter of sufficient importance to grant a certificate, then as I say, we take a neutral stance.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you, Ms. Korner. Anything else? Now, Madam, there must have either been a major collision on the way. But our secretaries were -- they were even ahead of me with all of my files and all the other files.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. Okay. Thank you. [Microphone not activated] Good morning to you, Judge. Please proceed with the usual solemn declaration with which you should be familiar by now. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning. I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. I thank you. You may sit down. Ms. Korner.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Yes. Could the witness be given back the first bundle of the Sanski Most documents. And if he could go to divider number 17.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Exhibit number, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Oh, I'm sorry. Exhibit P605.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Now, Judge, if you could find the version --

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Just to remind us, yesterday, Your Honour, we looked at Exhibit P601, which was a decision about establishing the Serbian municipality of Sanski Most. And this is very similar, but it's slightly different. And there's one matter I want to ask about. And this is -- it's the same date, the 25th of March, as the other document seemed to have at the end of it.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Judge, in this -- they're giving reasons for the adoption of the decision by the Serbian people of Sanski Most. And it states this in the second paragraph: "The Serbian people on the territory of Sanski Most municipality are not a minority. They make up a majority of the population and number 29.857 ethnic Serbs." Don't worry about the figures. We have them from the census ourselves. But then it goes on to say that "The total surface area of the municipality is 948 square kilometres, while the surface area inhabited by the Serbian population which has declared itself in favour of entering the Serbian Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina amounts to 70.6 per cent of the total surface area of the municipality." Now, I don't want to enter into percentages, Judge, at all, but in your view with your knowledge of this municipality, was that an accurate representation of the territory occupied by the Serbian people?

utterances.speaker: ADIL DRAGANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I know -- and I think that I am familiar with the data concerning the territory in Bosnia and Herzegovina -- I believe that these data are incorrect.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Wait. Okay. Go ahead.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: ADIL DRAGANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think that the data here are incorrect and arbitrary. It is correct that the surface of the municipality of Sanski Most is approximately 980 square kilometres.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: I'm sorry, pause. Did you say 980? Because it says here 948. Was that an accurate translation?

utterances.speaker: ADIL DRAGANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: ADIL DRAGANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is -- the thing that is written here is correct. This is what the Serbian authorities wrote. But the actual surface is about 983 square kilometres.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: I see. All right. And you say that as far as you're concerned to allege that 70.6 per cent is Serbian is inaccurate.

utterances.speaker: ADIL DRAGANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That would be absurd. It's incorrect, because in Bosnia and Herzegovina Bosniaks are in the majority --

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: ADIL DRAGANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Muslims.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: I think --

utterances.speaker: ADIL DRAGANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: But in our municipality, in the municipality of Sanski Most, I know that the majority population in Sanski Most in accordance with the 1999 census and throughout the history, it's been the Bosniaks. They had the majority.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: ADIL DRAGANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: So in 1992, before the beginning of the aggression on Sanski Most, I can give you the percentages and the ratio of the population. Do I have to?

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: No. We have the figures ourselves. Thank you very much. All right. That's all I want to ask you about that document. Could you move now, please --

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU-IVANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Madam Fauveau.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU-IVANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] For the transcript. I would now like to make an objection to this document and to any other document not bearing a signature. We also would like to challenge this document because its source is the state security service in Bihac.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated] I'm sorry. This document --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I thank you, Madam Fauveau.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Just pause. Thank you very much. This document in fact was part of the seizure from the Banja Luka CSB. It's not -- doesn't come from Bihac. I just want to make that clear.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU-IVANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm sorry, but we got a list from the Prosecution indicating the source of the document. And on that list, it is written "SDB Bihac" 17th of November, 1995.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ...

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: However, Judge, this came from Bihac. But do you know anything about this document? Had you seen it before you came to this court?

utterances.speaker: ADIL DRAGANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think that we looked at another document here, a document that was signed.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: ADIL DRAGANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: By the president of the Serbian democratic party, Vrkes Vlado, the president of the municipal assembly of Sanski Most, Nedeljko Rasula, and the president of the assemblement [As interpreted] club, Savonovic Boro. And that's the same document. It's virtually the same.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: I understand that. We've just gone back to that one. But this particular document, had you seen it before it went to the Bihac office if you can remember? If you can't remember, say so.

utterances.speaker: ADIL DRAGANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think that I saw this document. And I probably handed it over to Bihac.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Thank you. All right. Can we now move, please, in the bundle to document P6 --

utterances.speaker: ADIL DRAGANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm sorry. If I may. I remember this statement of reasons here quite well and this decision, and I do have the original in Sanski Most.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: One moment. The original of this particular exhibit that you have been shown? In other words, without a proper signature and without a proper stamp? Or with the proper signature and a proper stamp?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I think I have this -- the original of this document without the signature and without a stamp.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: All right. Could we move, please, to document marked Prosecutor's Exhibit 613, which we will find behind tab number 29. Now, this is a document dated the 14th of April, 1992 in -- from the CSB in Banja Luka -- or to the CSB, I think, from an operative, headed "Evaluation of the current security situation in the Sanski Most area," dealing -- saying that: "According to sources, the security situation in Sanski Most is complex and characterised by the law being ignored, frosty inter-ethnic relations, tension leading to the organisation of the population for self-protection, a rise in crime, and difficult internal affairs working conditions." And it says that is the reason is because of what's been happening all through Bosnia. But this paragraph: "The most recent incident of a mass gathering of armed Serbian and Muslim inhabitants in Sanski Most caused by explosives being placed on a building belonging to a Serb led to demands for the territory of the municipality to be divided." And then: "In order to improve the security situation, in addition to the engagement of mixed JNA and OUP patrols -- internal affairs patrols, it is necessary to devote other relevant attention in order to avert possible large scale excesses." Now, do you recall anything about an incident of a mass gathering of armed Serbs and Muslims and explosives being placed on a building belonging to a Serb around April of 1992?

utterances.speaker: ADIL DRAGANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I remember what the situation was like in April.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: ADIL DRAGANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: And in May.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: You've described to us the situation. I'm just asking do you have any recollection of any such incident as is described here?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: There are two incidents, Judge, that have been mentioned in this document and by Ms. Korner. Let's take the first one. Explosives being placed on a building belonging to a Serb. It doesn't say that it did explode. It just says that explosives were placed. Do you recall such an incident prior or -- around but certainly prior to 14th April 1992?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, I do remember that I carried out an on-site investigation, because at that time I was both the investigating judge and the President of the court. And in April and May, 44 explosions happened due to explosives being put on Croat and Muslim buildings, business premises, and houses. 44 is the exact number of such incidents.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And whether this was a situation -- you mentioned the 8th. There was an incident involving the placing of explosives, but I wasn't given any official reports about it. There was a cafe where Serb soldiers gathered. They went there every day and every night. They were armed. And that was in the immediate vicinity of the courthouse, across the road from it. I know that -- I think that the name of the owner was Lazic. He was a member of the SOS or -- I don't know. But I did not receive any official reports about the explosives being placed there, and I cannot confirm whether there had been any rallies of armed groups or any excesses, because at that time the Serbian army was present everywhere. There were checkpoints. You see what I mean. We were virtually invisible.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: One moment, Judge. Listen, I asked you a very simple question: Do you recall an incident around but certainly before the 14th of April, 1992, when allegedly explosives were placed on a building belonging to a Serb? Please answer me "yes" or "no" for the time being. It's not a question of whether you were informed officially or whether you read about it. It's a question of whether you heard that there was such an incident.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I do recall.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Now, on this occasion when these explosives were discovered on a building belonging to a Serb, do you recall a mass gathering of armed Serbs and Muslim -- Serbian and Muslim inhabitants in Sanski Most? Obviously related, in connection to the discovery of these explosives.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I think that there were no mass rallies.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Not mass rallies. Mass gatherings. I mean, it may be a question of interpretation. I -- unfortunately I can't follow both languages.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I did not notice any such thing.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. Please go ahead, Ms. Korner.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated] Okay. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Sorry.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Could you leave that document and go, please, to the document behind divider number 31, which is Prosecutor's Exhibit 614. Now, this is a document that comes from the files of the 1st Krajina Corps -- the 5th, as it then was -- dated the 19th of April, 1992. And under item 3, "situation in the area of responsibility." "The situation in our area of responsibility is still complex, particularly in the Sanski Most -- I think it must be -- area, where there has been a division of the police force." Was it around this time that, as you told us, the Serb police force was set up?

utterances.speaker: ADIL DRAGANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have already mentioned this in my testimony.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: ADIL DRAGANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: On the 19th of April, 1992 the Serb police was established -- or in other words, Bosniaks and Croats were simply expelled from the public security station.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Okay. The next -- it's the next line, then. I just want you to confirm it was around this date. "Thanks to the efforts of military organs and mixed patrol, there have been no clashes." First question: Were you aware of -- if it means that, and it may not -- mixed patrols of military and police being carried out?

utterances.speaker: ADIL DRAGANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have already spoke about that in my testimony, that the police officers of Bosniak and Croat ethnic origin were expelled on that day from the public security station, and they went to the building of the Municipal Assembly of Sanski Most, where they remained --

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: ADIL DRAGANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: -- Holding that building.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Yes. I -- all I'm concerned about is after the Muslims and Croats were expelled, whether then mixed police patrols with military -- I mean, i.e. Serb police patrols with military police patrols.

utterances.speaker: ADIL DRAGANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, they were made up of exclusively Serb police officers and military police officers. And at the -- checkpoints at the exit routes, I would see them from time to time or for a certain period of time.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Okay. Can we then move, please, to the next document, which is immediately following, Prosecutor's Exhibit P615, which is a Crisis Staff Sanski Most -- it looks like press release, I suppose, because it's dated the 20th of April, 1992 and addressed to the chief of public security service Banja Luka and the Serbian newspaper agency in Sarajevo and -- telling citizens that from the 20th of April, the territory in the Serbian municipality of Sanski Most, only the Serbian republic laws and regulations are valid. It guarantees peace and security to all citizens regardless of their religion, ethnicity, or ideology. And finally says this that "The Crisis Staff is of the opinion that force had to be used during the liberation of the Sanski Most Municipal Assembly building from the armed formations of the extreme faction of the SDA leadership. Long and exhausting talks simply failed to bear fruit -- and we call upon citizens to express their loyalty." Just very simple question, because you've told us -- you've described the takeover. Were there armed formations of the SDA in the municipal assembly building?

utterances.speaker: ADIL DRAGANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have already said that these were the police officers -- professional police officers from the public security station who had been expelled from there. The SDA did not have any armed formations in Sanski Most. There were only the police officers there, the ones who had gone over from the public security station and remained there for only two days.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: ADIL DRAGANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: And the leadership of the SDA party was also there -- some of the leaders of the party were also there. I think it was on the 18th, since these events took place on the 17th. And on the 18th, in the morning hours, I came in my car to the municipal assembly building to see what was going on, and they were in effect in the -- I was in fact in the building for half an hour, and I spoke to some people there. Then I left the building and went away.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Were any of the leaders that you've described of the SDA armed?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated] That he could see.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Oh, that he could see. Yes, obviously.

utterances.speaker: ADIL DRAGANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: They were wearing civilian clothes. They didn't have any weapons.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: All right. Can we move, then, please, to the very next document, Prosecutor's Exhibit P616. It's again a document that comes from the files of the Krajina Corps, dated the same day as this press release, the 20th of April. And if you go, please, to item number 2. It talks about the disposition of the 5th Corps and its zone of responsibility. "The activities of the corps command have centred on monitoring the situation in subordinated units and in the zone of responsibility. A team from corps command headed by the commander has assessed the situation in the Prijedor region, focussing on Sanski Most, and measures are being taken to improve the situation." Now, you've described the visit by General Talic, which was around this period of time. But were you aware, first of all, that there was a team, if you like, a number of officers in the Sanski Most region assessing what was happening? If the answer is no, say so.

utterances.speaker: ADIL DRAGANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I knew that the concentration of the armed forces of the Banja Luka Corps. And that's the corps that was under the command of General Talic. I knew that this corps surrounded Sanski Most. And on periphery of Sanski Most itself -- it was present on the periphery. I had important duties to carry out, as the President of the court. I was able to gain information about many things, and I was able to observe many things. And it was at that time that large columns of military vehicles of what was then the JNA came to Sanski Most and drove around in the middle of the day with the Serbian flag upfront. And there were dozens of vehicles. I counted them. On one Monday, there were over 80 vehicles of the JNA in a column in the middle of the town. They crossed the square. That was a demonstration of force, and it made the Muslims and Croats afraid. I was able to know about this. I saw high-ranking officers there too, because I was still in the court and I was in contact with the public security station. I would go to that station. I wasn't afraid. I was able to see and to meet high-ranking officers who were going up -- upstairs to where the command was. I knew very well that -- I knew very well what the military staff was doing, headed by Colonel [Realtime transcript read in error "Ganicic"] Anicic. I knew where the 6th Krajina Brigade was located, whose commander was Basara Branko. I had contact with Basara Branko because I was a member of the league of peace. And I -- we invited the command of the 6th Krajina Corps to a meeting, Basara, and he came.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: I'm sorry. It was translated -- it's come up on the screen as you knew very well what the military staff was doing, headed by -- headed by Colonel Ganicic. Do you mean Ganicic or Anicic?

utterances.speaker: ADIL DRAGANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's not Galicic. I said Anicic. Nedeljko Anicic, who was a colonel in the staff.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: I'm sorry. I appreciate that. The trouble is if we don't correct it now, it comes up in the transcript wrongly. All right. Thank you very much. Could you move to the next document, please, which is Prosecutor's Exhibit 617, which is at the next divider. It's a report from the -- of the Krajina Corps for the same date, 20th of April. Item number 3, "Situation on the territory -- in the zone of responsibility. The situation in the zone of responsibility continues to get more complex. Ethnic divisions have particularly escalated in Sanski Most, where there was sporadic shooting between Muslims -- Serbs and Muslims during the night in which the municipal assembly building was set on fire." And "There have been no conflicts during the day, and certain measures are being taken by the 5th Corps command and the Prijedor garrison to overcome the situation." Now, you've described to us in detail what happened. All I want to know is this: Was there actually shooting going on between Serbs and Muslims after the municipal building was attacked?

utterances.speaker: ADIL DRAGANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The army fired at the municipal building from a -- a military personal carrier which was positioned on the square. They used a --

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: ADIL DRAGANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: -- A megaphone and asked the policemen to come out. No one fired from the municipality building. There was no resistance. There was -- not a single bullet was fired.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you. Okay. Could we move then, please --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: One moment, because I don't think that the answer -- reply is comprehensive. The statement in this document said that there was sporadic shooting between Serbs and Muslims during the night in which the municipal assembly building was set on fire. You certainly recall the night in which the municipal assembly building was set on fire. Now, before or after that the municipal assembly building was set on fire or even during the time when it was set on fire, do you recall any sporadic shooting between Serbs and Muslims? Not necessarily between the army and the police that were in the building. The events of those -- of that particular night. Do you recall any sporadic shooting between Serbs and Muslims?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I've understood you. I was clear. There was no shooting between the Muslims and the Serbs. The Serbs fired that evening.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you. Ms. Korner.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Well, I think -- Your Honour, just to make it absolutely clear, because I see the point Your Honour's making.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Other than -- within the precinct of the municipal building and what was happening there, was there any shooting going on elsewhere in the town that you're aware of between Serbs and Muslims?

utterances.speaker: ADIL DRAGANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I remember that evening very well. There was shooting but not between the Muslims and the Serbs. The military formations and the police who had weapons were involved in the shooting, and that was in the centre of the town itself.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: All right. Are we talking about military -- Serb military against Muslim police officers?

utterances.speaker: ADIL DRAGANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: ADIL DRAGANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: And that lasted for about -- well, from 9.00 in the evening until 11.00. And then nothing else was heard. I saw that. I was in my parents' house that evening. I wasn't able to stay in my own house. My father and I were there.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Next question, Ms. Korner.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Don't worry. All that I -- I just want to make it absolutely clear. This was an incident separate -- this was an incident separate from the attack on the municipal building that you're talking about.

utterances.speaker: ADIL DRAGANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This was not an incident, but this is something I saw. When the shooting on the square was heard -- and this was not far from my house -- at that point, the crossroads were blocked. A lorry with a trailer arrived just above my house by the crossroads, and they blocked the bridge. The lorry with the trailer arrived. I know who brought it, who drove it up. It was a Serbian neighbour from an adjacent street. And the entrance to the city was blocked. This is what I wanted to say. And the checkpoint remained there. And when I was arrested, the checkpoint was still there.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Okay. Final question on this, and I hope we're getting -- is what happened to the Muslim police officers who were firing at the Serb military?

utterances.speaker: ADIL DRAGANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The Muslim policemen didn't shoot at the Serbian soldiers. They didn't. I'll repeat this. The Muslim policemen who were on the other side of the building, they simply left the building on the other side. There was a -- a side exit. And they went along the bank of the Sana River.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Okay?

utterances.speaker: ADIL DRAGANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: They all took this route to leave in the direction of Sehovci, a village which was about 2 kilometres away. It's a Muslim village. That's where they went in the evening.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Okay. Fine. I'm sorry. It's entirely my fault -- and it may be Your Honours have understood -- who was the shooting -- that you said there was shooting away from the municipal building between Muslims and Serbs. Who was doing the shooting?

utterances.speaker: ADIL DRAGANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the municipality building, soldiers were firing from the square at the windows, at the doors. And members of the SOS and probably members of the Serbian police, they were firing in the direction of the building. All the officers -- the walls in all the offices had potholes, had holes in the walls.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: No. Please stop, Judge, for a moment. I'm not interested in the municipal building at the moment. I understood your evidence when we looked at this entry in the 1st KK - Krajina Corps - document, you agreed that that was sporadic shooting between Serbs and Muslims somewhere in the town. You don't agree.

utterances.speaker: ADIL DRAGANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't agree.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: All right. In that case, I think we're back to square one, and I'm going to leave it?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Leave it. Next question, Ms. Korner, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Can we go then, please, to the next document. And very briefly, it's really just to note in passing that -- I'm sorry. P618. It's the same incident effectively. In item 3 "Situation in the territory." Again, a Krajina Corps document dated the 21st of April. "The situation in Sanski Most remains critical, and the corps command is already taking measures to overcome the current situation." And effectively you've described what that -- those measures were. So could we move, please, to the next document, Prosecutor's Exhibit P619, at divider 36. Yes. Now, just for a moment -- this document comes from -- was submitted by Bihac to the Office of the Prosecutor. But you've described how you found various documents from the Crisis Staff when you returned to Sanski Most. Was this one of them, can you recall? If you can have a very quick look at it.

utterances.speaker: ADIL DRAGANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's one of the documents.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Thank you. Where were all these documents relating to these decisions of the Crisis Staff found?

utterances.speaker: ADIL DRAGANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: And where were they?

utterances.speaker: ADIL DRAGANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You're referring to these documents?

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Yes. The documents that relate to conclusions of the Crisis Staff or Crisis Staff documents, where were they found?

utterances.speaker: ADIL DRAGANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Sanski Most, in the premises of the municipality, in the Crisis Staff.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Okay. Now, I just want to look at a couple of these conclusions here. First of all, conclusion number 3, "Rasula and Anicic are hereby instructed to visit the leadership of the Autonomous Region of Krajina and explain in detail the situation in Sanski Most and try to obtain suggestions and guidelines for further action." And then at the bottom, item number 9: "We recommend to all citizens of Sanski Most municipality who have displayed extremism in working against the Serbian people to refrain from coming to work in the coming days for their own safety." Now, do you recall any announcements or any instructions being publicly made to that effect?

utterances.speaker: ADIL DRAGANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know that at that time, during that period -- and that was in the second half of April and the first half of May -- I know that during that period people were dismissed from their jobs, people who were Bosniaks, of Bosniak nationality, and of Croatian nationality were dismissed. And in institutions, organs, and companies --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Judge, be patient. One moment, please. The question was something completely different. And in a way Ms. Korner is to blame for this because she referred to two paragraphs that have got absolutely nothing to do, the one with the other. Let's start with the latter of these two paragraphs, number 9: "We recommend to all citizens of Sanski Most municipality who have displayed extremism in working against Serbian people to refrain from coming to work in the coming days for their own safety." The question was: Do you recall any announcement or any instructions being publicly -- I repeat, publicly -- made to this effect or to that effect? Please answer "yes" or "no." If it's yes, then do give us the details as to the -- the kind of announcement that you're referring to that, you heard.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I can't remember an announcement being made, but I do remember that people would lose their jobs. They were quite simply told that they shouldn't turn up to their jobs.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. Stop there. And the other one was -- the other paragraph, paragraph 3 is: "Nedeljko Rasula and Nedzo Anicic are hereby instructed to visit the leadership of the Autonomous Region of Krajina and explain in detail the situation in Sanski Most and try to obtain suggestions and guidelines for further action." Do you recall having heard or seen public announcement to that effect?

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Well, Your Honour -- well, you can ask the question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. Well, it was part of the question.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: No. It wasn't, actually. You're quite right. I looked at my question, and it was unclear. I merely noted that in passing, and I was merely asking about that. But as Your Honours asked the question -- I doubt it, but --

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Were you aware of visits by the leadership of the Crisis -- or in this case the leader of the Crisis Staff, or one of them, and Colonel Anicic to the Autonomous Region leadership?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Are you aware of it; yes or no?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I don't remember that visit. I -- it's not something that I followed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Next question.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'd just like to add something. I'll just be brief. The conclusions of the Crisis Staff weren't made public knowledge, not all of them were made public knowledge.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... okay. Please go ahead, Ms. Korner.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Now, can we move, please, now to Prosecutor's Exhibit P621, which is behind divider 38.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Ms. Korner, if you could kindly restrict your questions or phrase them in a way as to ask for a yes or no reply, answer, that would be much better I think.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Well, I hoped that they were.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: And you have been trying to. And perhaps the witness understands what I'm saying, and we could move along that way.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Okay. This is conclusions of the Crisis Staff, dated the 22nd of April, 1992. In paragraph number 4, Rasula is tasked with going with some other gentleman, the acting director of the public auditing service to Banja Luka and bringing all documents relating to the redirection of the transfer of payments to the SDK of the Autonomous Region of Krajina. Now, I just want you to confirm -- is this right -- I think you told us about it -- that -- that when the SDK had earlier been taken over and your salary came through Banja Luka, if you got paid.

utterances.speaker: ADIL DRAGANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's right. Salaries were transferred through Banja Luka, but we hadn't received our salaries since February.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: All right. And then at the bottom, paragraph 7: "Boro and Vlado are hereby tasked with contacting representatives of the Muslim and Croatian peoples and requesting that they be loyal to the existing organs of authority of the Serbian municipality of Sanski Most and conveying them -- to them that they will be guaranteed all rights in employment, civil, religious, and other equalities." Again, simple question, were you contacted by either of these gentlemen -- I've forgotten who Boro is -- as a representative of the Muslims and asked --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. But was -- are you presuming that he was a representative of the Muslims?

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: As a judge and as a presiding President of the court, I mean, I find it strange that you are addressing him as a possible representative of the Muslim people there -- then, you know, or --

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: You do?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Because a representative of the Muslim or Croatian people to me has got a political connotation.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Well, Your Honour, I don't know what the answer to that is so -- I'll ask him.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Were you considered -- if you can answer that question, I suppose -- to be a representative of the Muslim people in Sanski Most in your position as a judge?

utterances.speaker: ADIL DRAGANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was someone who had been invested with authority on behalf of all the people, not just the Muslim people.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: ADIL DRAGANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was a judge for all the peoples.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: And then perhaps you can ask him the question, because the Chamber would be interested in knowing, whether there was a follow-up to this, whether, in other words, these two [Realtime transcript read in error "villages"] individuals, Boro and Vlado -- Vlado, I suppose it's --

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Vrkes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Vrkes. Boro, I don't know -- Boro Savanovic, yes?

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Savanovic, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Whether you are aware, Judge, that these two persons in compliance with this task that was -- they were entrusted with did actually contact to your knowledge representatives of the Muslim and Croatian people, putting the request that is indicated in this last paragraph, 7, on this document. That you know of.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] After the 20th --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, after the 20th.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] -- As far as I know, there was no more contact. And the SDA and HDZ party weren't visible any more. As far as I know, there were no conversations about these -- about this subject.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Next question, Ms. Korner.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Well, Your Honour, I think the --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Ackerman.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: There's a transcript problem, Your Honour, with your question. It says: "The two villages Boro and Vlado" -- they're not villages. They're people.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you, Mr. Ackerman.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Your Honour, I think in fact the next witness might be better able to deal with that rather than this witness. All right. Can we move to Prosecutor's Exhibit P622, which is after divider 40. In fact, this is dated the 23rd of April, 1st Krajina Corps document -- or 5th, as it then was. Under item 3, "Situation on the ground." "The situation in the areas where excesses occurred is now under control and the visit of the Corps Commander to the Sanski Most and his tour today of Habjanovci have had a calming effect on the situation." It's clearly -- it refers to the visit that you've described of General Talic. Simply, yes or no, as far as you were concerned, did his visit have the effect of calming, as it's put here, the situation in Sanski Most?

utterances.speaker: ADIL DRAGANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't notice that.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Please, then, can we move to document -- Prosecutor's Exhibit 625, which we will find behind divider 44. This is a report by this man Milos, dated the 24th of April, 1992, which states this: "After members of the Territorial Defence, the Serbian police and volunteers had taken all key installations in Sanski Most. Almost all extreme members of the SDA fled Sanski Most. Most escaped to Croatia, where they earlier built summer houses." Now, forget about whether there were summer houses or not. But after the takeover, did members of the SDA, the leaders, flee Sanski Most?

utterances.speaker: ADIL DRAGANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I remember, no leaders of the SDA fled. They all remained in Sanski Most, as far as the municipal board is concerned.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Okay. Can we --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Any information about the origin of this document? What --

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: It comes from the CSB in Banja Luka, Your Honour. It's one of these documents we had a long discussion about. There's an --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Perhaps the witness could give us some information. I would imagine, Madam Fauveau, you are objecting to the -- please.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU-IVANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. I have a general objection I would like to make. The document doesn't have a signature or stamp, but the witness didn't answer the question because the question was about the members of the SDA. And the witness -- the witness's response concerned the leaders of the SDA.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. She's -- Madam Fauveau is right.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Yes. Well, I didn't imagine it mattered -- well, okay.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Leaving aside the municipal board, are you aware of -- well, I don't know about extreme members -- members of the SDA fleeing to Croatia?

utterances.speaker: ADIL DRAGANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is very difficult to answer the question, but let me say briefly that at that time the population of Sanski Most took their families away to safe places and left. And in April and in May, three or four thousands of people, families mostly, family members, left the area. It is quite difficult to say now whether these were SDA members, because there were over a thousand members of the SDA, at least. I know quite a few SDA members who didn't go anywhere. But there may be those who did go with their families.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Next question, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Your Honour, I am moving as quickly as I can.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. No. I ...

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Right. Can we move to the next document, please, Prosecutor's Exhibit 626, which is behind the next divider.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Don't take my invitation to the next question to proceed to the next question as a criticism, Ms. Korner.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Well, no. I just notice that Your Honour was saying "next question" quite a lot this morning.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Right. This is again a Crisis Staff conclusion dated the 28th of April. Item 1: "All citizens in the area of Sanski Most municipality who possess any kind of weapon shall hand it in to the public security station, the closest unit of the JNA, or the staff of the Territorial Defence of the Serbian municipality of Sanski Most. Citizens should hand in weapons by 1900 hours," and so on and so forth. "Citizens who have private weapons with a licence from a competent organ and members of armed Territorial Defence formations, active service, and reserve police, and the Yugoslav People's Army are exempt from this decision." Now, we -- you've dealt in your evidence with the announcement of the surrender of weapons. What I want to ask is this: Citizens who have private weapons with a licence from a competent organ. As a judge, what was the competent organ to issue the licence?

utterances.speaker: ADIL DRAGANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The competent organ was the public security station, which issued licences to carry pistols or hunting rifles.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Okay. This announcement purports to say that anyone who has such a licence for a private weapon will be allowed to keep their weapons. Was that actually applied to the Muslim and Croat populations who held licenced weapons?

utterances.speaker: ADIL DRAGANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This decision was broadcast on several occasions on the radio, on the Serbian radio, and I was able to hear it. But both legal and illegal weapons had to be registered. That's what it said on the radio.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Okay. So were -- I mean, very simply yes or no -- were Muslims and Croats who held licensed weapons permitted to keep them?

utterances.speaker: ADIL DRAGANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, they were not allowed to keep them. Weapons were taken away from them, and people were in fact beaten because of that and imprisoned.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Thank you. Could we move then to the next document, please, which is the following divider. It's marked Exhibit P164. It's dated the 29th of April, 1992 "Conclusions of the Crisis Staff meeting." "That changes be made and all officials of the lower court of the Serbian municipality of Sanski Most be appointed as acting officials. Vrkes, Vrucinic, and Nikolic are in charge." If I understand this correctly, what it's saying is that anybody who holds a position will no longer have an official but merely an acting position. Is that how it happened? Is that what you were told?

utterances.speaker: ADIL DRAGANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. The sense of this conclusion is that all those who held posts of a manager or a director of Muslim and Croat ethnicity would be replaced and that new acting officials would be put in these posts, because it says here in item 2 that the director of the Sanski Most public utilities public enterprise be replaced. That was a Muslim, Ahmet Paunovic. So he was replaced at that time. And an acting official -- an acting manager was put on that post. He was a Serb. And Lukic, who was the manager at the same time, was put in charge of this.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Yes. Can I -- it may be that it's -- it's a translation problem, because it doesn't say that the officials at the lower court in our translation must be replaced. It says they must be appointed as acting. Is that an accurate translation? Leave aside what actually happened.

utterances.speaker: ADIL DRAGANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It seems that the translation is wrong, because what it says here is that changes be made and that all officials at the lower court of the Serbian municipality of Sanski Most be appointed as acting officials. Vrkes, Vrucinic, and Nikolic are in charge.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: I'm sorry. Okay. In any event, I think you've told us the result was eventually you were all removed. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ADIL DRAGANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In item 3, it says here -- well, the director was also a Bosniak, Sabanovic, Enis, a doctor. And Dr. Grubisa, a Serb was put on that post instead. That happened then. And also Radovan Stanic replaced me in the court. And in the misdemeanours court, Nedzad Muhic was replaced by Ms. Andja Vujanic.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Yes. You've told us. All right. Can we move then, please, to the next document, which is Prosecutor's Exhibit P -- well, we could just note. If you look at the next document, P627, we see there in item number 3 the doctor that you've referred to taking over. However, can we move -- the next document I want to ask you about, Prosecutor's Exhibit 630, which we will find behind divider 50.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: I'm not -- I'm just noting this because it shows the change. Item one --

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: I'm not going to ask you a question. The Crisis Staff of the Sanski Most Serbian municipality shall operate as a war staff as of today, purely showing, as I opened the case, the changes in name. But item number 5, please, on that list: "Radovan Stanic, Sanski Most lower court judge, shall be in charge of preparing and setting up a wartime court in accordance with the state of war declared in the Autonomous Region of Krajina." And you showed -- you found and produced for us the actual official decision so appointing him. Item number 9. "The existing checkpoint at the gas station at Tomina shall be moved and a new one set up at the Vrhpolje bridge." Do you recall a checkpoint being set up at the bridge, at around this period of time?

utterances.speaker: ADIL DRAGANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do remember. I was going in the direction of Kljuc.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: And Your Honours, finally over the page -- it's not really asking a question. But while we're looking at this document, the paragraph that begins: "In the spirit of the conclusions of the meeting of the war staff of the Autonomous Region of Krajina held on the 6th of May, the Crisis Staff of the Sanski Most Serbian municipality accepts and orders the implementation of the following conclusions." Your Honour, I'm not going to refer back to -- there's a decision of the 6th of May from the Autonomous Region.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Okay. Can we move on them, please, to Prosecutor's Exhibit P634, which we will find behind divider number 5 -- sorry -- yes. And it goes -- we're back into -- 5. Actually -- I'm sorry, Your Honour. I don't know why I mentioned -- it's a straight order. And I must have had a reason, but I can't remember what it was at the moment. It's just an order to disarm paramilitary formations. Could we move then, please, to Prosecutor's Exhibit 636. I'm sorry. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Your Honour -- yes. 635. If we could just look at that in passing, dated the 20th of May.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Item number 7. At the request of the regional Crisis Staff, the Crisis Staff of the Serbian municipality appointed Vlado Vrkes, deputy president of the Crisis Staff of the Sanski Most Serbian municipality." But then if we move to Prosecutor's Exhibit 636. And just really -- it was a meeting of the fourth session of the executive committee of the Sanski Most Municipal Assembly. But I think this is a document, Judge, that you directly handed to a member of the Office of the Prosecutor in April of 1996. Were these documents all in the municipal assembly building as well? It's of no interest otherwise at the moment.

utterances.speaker: ADIL DRAGANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct. They were in the building of the municipality of Sanski Most in a binder.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: All right. Can we move, then, please to the next document, P -- Prosecutor's Exhibit P637. A Crisis Staff conclusion of the 22nd of May, 1992. Item F: "Boro and Vlado will be responsible for the work of the judiciary in wartime conditions." Now, I just want to ask you one question: Before these events, did the municipal assembly have any control over the workings of judges, how the judges operated and their workings?

utterances.speaker: ADIL DRAGANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: We submitted reports on our work, on the work of the judiciary to the municipal assembly. Although we were an independent judicial organ of Bosnia and Herzegovina, the Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Did -- could the municipal assembly order you to do certain things in connection with carrying out your function as a judge? In other words, to release people or imprison people or matters of that nature.

utterances.speaker: ADIL DRAGANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think they could not have issued any such orders to me and to other judges -- neither could they do so to other judges. But at that time the situation was different because I no longer had any control over the Serbian judges.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: No. No. Absolutely. That's what I mean. Before these events in April of 1992, were you ever given instructions or interfered with in that respect by the municipal assembly?

utterances.speaker: ADIL DRAGANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't think so. We were independent -- an independent organ. And in accordance to the law, we had to submit yearly or periodical reports on our work. And then this was discussed at a session of the municipal assembly. Other than that, nobody could order us to do anything of this sort. I'm now talking about the period before the events, before 1992.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: ADIL DRAGANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: And in fact, nobody could order me to do anything up until the very time when I was replaced.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: All right. And then if you could just turn over the page. Item number 4 -- and this is the 22nd of May, 1992. As far --

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: No. No. It's all right. He can just follow on.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Item number 4 in the same document: "As far as disarming paramilitary formations in Sanski Most is concerned, Colonel Basara and Colonel Anicic are charged with putting this into practice." Now, very simple question: Were you aware on the 22nd of May of paramilitary forces in Sanski Most? In other words, Muslim or Croat forces.

utterances.speaker: ADIL DRAGANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I know, there weren't any. I think there weren't any.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Ackerman.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Your Honour, the -- the paragraph says "paramilitary formations," it did you want say Muslim or Croat paramilitary formations.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, you are right, Mr. Ackerman.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Oh, I agree, Your Honour. But there's absolutely not one iota of evidence that anybody else other than --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Ackerman. Please --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Wait. Please finish what you are saying, Ms. Korner, and then Mr. Ackerman will have his say as well.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: If the suggestion is that this refers to Serbian paramilitary forces, Your Honour, there's not one iota of evidence that this order and all other orders reply to anything other than Muslim and Croat.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Ackerman.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Your Honour, my objection -- I didn't invite Ms. Korner to testify -- there were significant numbers of Serb paramilitary formations that were seeking to be disarmed. So now I've testified. But they were trying to disarm Serb paramilitary formations. That was happening all across the country.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Your Honour, I'm talking about evidence that has been called in this case so far, not evidence that will or may be called. But in any event, I will ask the question --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, please do.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: -- In all forms.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: First, were there any paramilitary formations that you are aware of which were either Muslim or Croat? Operating in Sanski Most on the 22nd of May?

utterances.speaker: ADIL DRAGANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know that there weren't any.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: All right. Were there, however, any Serb paramilitary forces operating in Sanski Most in -- on the 22nd of May?

utterances.speaker: ADIL DRAGANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: "Paramilitary," that's a term that I would like to explain a little bit. Everything was under the control of the military command of the 6th Brigade -- Krajina Brigade in Sanski Most. Now, whether the SOS was a paramilitary unit, perhaps it was. But it was under the command, and they did things together and they had a joint command. There weren't any other forces.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you. Next question.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Can we move --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Perhaps, Ms. Korner -- I mean, we are approaching the break time.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Whenever it's convenient.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Your Honour, it's convenient now. Can I say I will complete my examination-in-chief before the next break.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you, Ms. Korner. We'll break for 30 minutes. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Yes. Could we move then, please, to the next document, which is behind divider number 9, P638. Now, this document is apparently approved by or comes from Colonel Anicic and is an order dated -- I'm not sure that we've got a date, but clearly before the 26th of May sometime. In paragraph number 1 -- oh, it's headed I'm sorry "Combat task disarmament operation in Sanski Most." In paragraph number 1, it refers to members of the HOS, the Croatian defence forces and Green Berets which were inserted earlier have joined up with hostile villages and towns in Sanski Most municipality. With their help they have managed to form eight detachments, five independent companies, and a number of independent platoons in Mahala and various other places. The enemies intensively inserting individuals for intelligence, reconnaissance, and sabotage tasks and in the unoccupied territory of the town and its surroundings." All I want to ask you about is Mahala, because that's where you were based. Were you aware of companies, platoons, operating in Mahala? If you could just answer "yes" or "no."

utterances.speaker: ADIL DRAGANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: All right. Now, in fact, this document appears to be part of the orders for the attack. If we go over the page, -- on our page, page 2 -- once the positions have been taken, use the Serbian Territorial Defence units to prevent the insertion/operation of sabotage group. And after artillery preparations, disarm the settlements of Mahala, Otoci, Muhici and Marije Bursac and other neighbourhoods in coordination with the 6th Brigade units in order to cause the enemy great human, material, and technical losses. "Stand by for the attack at 0500 on the 26th of May. Start of the attack at specific signal." And then can we look just at paragraph 6. "The first Serbian battalion has the task of organising the defence of Serbian populated areas in the sectors. And it names a number of streets. Could you have for a moment -- are those streets in the Sanski Most town itself or elsewhere?

utterances.speaker: ADIL DRAGANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: These streets are in Sanski Most, in the town.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: All right. Just very quickly, could we have a look at the map again of Sanski Most, which is Prosecutor's Exhibit 757.1.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Your Honour, it's the one with the photographs on the side. And there's a spare copy if ...

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Yes. If you could just indicate with the pointer where the -- those streets are roughly.

utterances.speaker: ADIL DRAGANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The area -- the Narodni front area is here, and this sports hall is located in that area. This is the Narodni front neighbourhood. These are the buildings you can see here. And this is Veljko Miljevic Street, which goes as far as the bridge, which -- this entire street is Veljko Miljevic Street. It's on the left bank of the Sana River. It's in the centre of the town. It's the central -- it's the main street.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: ADIL DRAGANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is the Narodni front neighbourhood, Alagica Polje neighbourhood is the neighbourhood here to the left -- on the left-hand side. This is Alagica Polje. In fact, Marije Bursac and Alagica Polje. Cvijo Kukolj Street is here in Alagica Polje. This is the one which goes through this -- which passes through this neighbourhood. That's the central part here.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: All right. Thank you. And then the paragraph goes on to say: "Upon completion of artillery operations, attack and search so as to cause the enemy the greatest possible losses in manpower, material, and equipment." And I think that's all we need look at in this document. Could we move then, please, to the next document now, which is Prosecutor's Exhibit P639, which is behind the next divider. And this is "Conclusions of the Crisis Staff, dated the 23rd of May." And in paragraph 3: "Issue a proclamation to the radio station --" I'm sorry. "The question of disarming paramilitary formations of armed individuals. Implement the conclusions from the previous Crisis Staff meeting. Issue a proclamation to the radio station on Saturday, the 23rd of May, 1992, to be read out every 20 minutes." Did you hear those announcements? Just "yes" or "no."

utterances.speaker: ADIL DRAGANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Thank you. Then could we move to Prosecutor's Exhibit, please, 641, which we can find behind divider 13. This is dated the -- or the stamp is the 6th of June. But if we look at the document, it appears to be dated the 26th of May. And "Pursuant to the conclusions of the Crisis Staff, the civilian protection municipal staff hereby issues the following: The displaced population which withdrew from the Mahala, Muhici, and Otoci settlements to the Krkojevci area is to be transferred by a San Trams [phoen] bus to the sports hall for care and consideration."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Accommodation.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Sorry. Accommodation.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Accommodation. Just very -- well, actually, no. I think I'll deal --

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: I'm sorry, Your Honour, I think I'll deal with this with another witness, because the witness can deal with the actual events of the sports hall. So can we move, please, to Prosecutor's Exhibit P642, a document from the Krajina Corps dated the 27th of May, 1992.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: And in the end of the first paragraph, it states: "The situation in Sanski Most is becoming increasingly complicated. At about 1500 hours in the area of Sanski Most, the Green Braise attacked a convoy of buses transporting conscripts, killing two conscripts and likely or seriously wounding roughly 20 others. The command of the 30th Partisan Division was ordered to send in a combat group to rescue the convoy." Now, I think this was the day of your arrest, was it not, Judge?

utterances.speaker: ADIL DRAGANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was arrested on the 25th of May, 1992.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: All right. In that case, you were already arrested. Do you know anything about this incident? Did you hear from any of the people who were brought into the prison anything about this incident, or any of the guards? If you didn't, say so straight away, please.

utterances.speaker: ADIL DRAGANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I really didn't hear anything about such an incident occurring in the area of Sanski Most.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Thank you. Then can we move, please, to the next document, which is P643, the same date. There are a series of documents about bodies that I just want to look at because of your exhumation activities. "Order, that the terrain in the area of Mahala, Otoci, and Muhici should be sanitised. In order to carry out this order, the following shall be done: Bodies must urgently be removed, identified, and buried in the designated place, a marked burial site. Somebody called Kljuicic and the burial service attached to the sanitation platoon in cooperation with the court and medical bodies assigned by the authorised organ shall be responsible for the carrying out of this order." Now, the people who were killed when these areas were attacked, were they buried in marked graves?

utterances.speaker: ADIL DRAGANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: They were buried in a mass grave in Greda.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: And was that -- was that marked?

utterances.speaker: ADIL DRAGANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It wasn't marked. It had been levelled with the ground. When we arrived there in 1995, the terrain was covered by grass. It had been levelled with the ground. There was -- there were no markings. And only some of the victims were there. There were two mass graves, in fact. We don't know where some of the bodies are. Some of the bodies of the people who were killed at the time.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Okay. Could we then move very briefly then to look at the next document, which is --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: One moment.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Sorry.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Ms. Korner, this document that we've just been referring to, Exhibit P643.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: It has a date which is the 27th of May, 1992.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Mm-hm.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: And it refers to a specific area of Mahala, Otoci, and Muhici. Does witness have an idea as to the number of persons that remained killed -- were killed in this area on or around the said date?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] About 46 people were killed on the 27th of May in that area. 13 people were killed in one house. They were mainly women and children.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. That's it. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Then -- it may be the next document that you can't help on either. Could we just look, however briefly, at Prosecutor's Exhibit P644, 28th of May -- actually, no. I'm sorry. I won't trouble, because it's definitely out of the --

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Your Honour, if we could just move -- Oh, yes. I'm sorry. Here we are.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: It's the paragraph 1: "In the Kljuc area, the situation has deteriorated. Muslims are carrying out organised actions conducting surprise and open attacks against military convoys and units moving along the axis of the Krasulje village to Sanski Most." Did you hear from anyone, either guards or fellow prisoners, about any of this when you were in the police station at Sanski Most? And again, if you didn't -- if you didn't, just say so straight away.

utterances.speaker: ADIL DRAGANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: When I found out about this incident when I arrived in the Manjaca camp.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Just very briefly, was there an attack as described?

utterances.speaker: ADIL DRAGANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: There was no attack. That was a Serbian checkpoint, and an incident occurred involving the inhabitants of Krasulje. All house there is are Muslim houses. The police erected -- set up a checkpoint there. And blocked the area and there was a conflict which broke out and people started shooting, and this policeman was killed on that occasion.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: All right. We can hear about that from --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. But the statement in the report, Judge, is very specific, and it refers to open attacks against military convoys and units moving. So we're not talking about a checkpoint, something stationary, but something which is moving, being either a unit or a military convoy. Can you enlighten us on this? Are you aware or were you aware at the time of any such open attacks by Muslims against such military convoys or moving units in the axis Krasulje area?

utterances.speaker: ADIL DRAGANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Up until the 25th of May, when I was arrested, and while I was in prison I did not hear about incidents of -- of that kind.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: ADIL DRAGANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't hear about people attacking a military convoy and shooting at it.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Your Honour, I think the question is better directed to other witnesses, so I'll leave that.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Could we move then, please, to Prosecutor's Exhibit 645, which is behind divider 17. Again -- and it refers to what you've already talked about. The 28th of May, 1992: "Decision, the so-called Greda Muslim cemetery has been designated for the burial of people killed in the Sanski Most municipality. Those killed should be buried in a communal grave in the presence of authorised officials without the usual rights, the presence of family members. Those killed should be labelled with metal tags. Each grave should be marked with a wooden plank --"

utterances.speaker: THE USHER
utterances.text: There's no B/C/S version.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: That's quite right. There isn't one in my bundle either. Your Honour, I'm sorry. I don't know what happened. We seem to have lost the B/C/S version there. Do Your Honours have it?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. We have it. Ms. Korner, I have a note on -- there must have been an incident on this document already because -- or else while I was sorting out the papers myself, because I have a personal note saying -- which I put "please replace P645 with this one." If I remember well, you had a previous 645 which you asked to replace, this being the B/C/S version

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: I don't -- I mean, I couldn't swear to it, Your Honour, but I can't imagine -- because we -- we only numbered these quite later on.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yeah. But it's -- definitely I had another 645 which had nothing to do presumably with this 645, which could have been my mistake. I mean, it's -- I'm not saying that -- or I'm not saying that it was a mistake in any case. But it certainly exists in the B/C/S version. I have it.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: All right. Well, if the registry have it -- no they probably don't, because they --

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: You can give mine to the witness.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Very grateful, Mr. Ackerman.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: It's marked -- for whatever it's worth, the top right you have "3.21" in the English version.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: But 3.24 in the B/C/S version. This is -- this is probably what happened. This is why --

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: It may be that that's right, Your Honour. It's gone somewhere else by mistake. But we'll -- we'll make sure that there are copies produced for the registry so they can mark it A and B in the normal way.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: In any event, if you've had a chance to read through that, Judge, it was said that they were to be labelled with metal tags and that there was a wooden plank bearing the identification number. When you came back on -- in 1995, do I take it that there was no indication of the number or the metal tags?

utterances.speaker: ADIL DRAGANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: When the exhumation of the Greda mass grave was carried out, I think there were 25 bodies in one of the mass graves. Metal tags were found there. They were the -- approximately 1 by 1 centimetre large, but there were no such tags in any other grave. I found these metal tags in the public utility company in Sanski Most, and I do have some of them.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: That's all right. I don't think -- you don't have it here though, do you?

utterances.speaker: ADIL DRAGANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I don't have them with me. But I did hand over a tag of this kind to one of the investigators of the Office of the Prosecutor in 1996. That was Mrs. Jutta.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Oh. Yes?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Judge, forget for the time being the exhumation site, the mass grave site, you referred to in your evidence already, but my question to you is a very simple one: Were any of the persons killed in the Sanski Most municipality at the time we're talking about, roughly end of May 1992, actually buried in the Greda Muslim cemetery? And if they were, are you aware or can you tell us whether the place, the tomb where they were buried, whether a wooden plank bearing the identification number of the deceased was placed there.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: I'm sorry, Your Honour --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: We're talking of the Greda Muslim cemetery. Not the exhumation site.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: No. He said earlier -- sorry, Your Honour -- when I dealt with the first document that that's where they were buried, the people who were killed in this particular cemetery.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Even the Greda mass grave.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: This is this is what he's talking about.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Where it was exhumed.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Was that part of the cemetery itself?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. But there were no markings, and nobody knew that it was there. It was part of the terrain where there were no graves. No bodies had been buried there previously.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I fail to understand. This Greda Muslim cemetery, how big was it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, approximately 100 metres by 150 metres.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: And it was used regularly before the conflict.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, that's right. That was the Muslim cemetery in the town.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: So was the mass grave then dug up inside the perimeters of the cemetery or outside?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, you could say that it was within the perimeter of the cemetery.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: And during this period, if, for example, you wanted to -- I don't know what's the custom in your country. But if you want to visit the grave site of your family in this cemetery, as we regularly do in my country, were you allowed free access to it or was that restrained or prohibited at the time?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] At that time access was prohibited. Muslims were prohibited from going to the cemetery, except subject to their approval. They would sometimes allow a burial to go on, but the number of people who were allowed to attend was limited to five and sometimes even less. That was the situation between 1992 and 1995.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: So the situation seems to be the following -- the position seems to be the following, that the people killed in Sanski Most municipality were actually buried inside the perimeters of Greda Muslim cemetery. There, as a result of the exhumations carried out, you did establish that the corpses had metal tags. The only thing that was missing is the wooden planks marking the site where each individual person killed was buried. That's the only thing that was missing, with the result that one would not be in a position to know where the burial site was, in other words.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The bodies had been collected in locations where the people were killed, and they were buried as they were, in a mass grave. They were put one next to another, and the length was 25 metres. The width was between 1 metre 50 and 2, and the depth was 2 metres 50 or 3 metres. And then the ground was levelled, and there were no markings.
